_comment: The Conditional Access checklist (Lib/Get-TPCAChecklist.ps1). Checks follow Maester's tests by id (MT.xxxx; the match rules are the tool's port of Maester's, with the differences named in the Lib file); templates are Microsoft's Conditional Access templates as report-only policy bodies for POST /identity/conditionalAccess/policies. The tool never creates a policy. @AdminRoles expands to the roles below; @SyncRole to the Directory Synchronization Accounts role; emergency-access exclusions come from the tenant's approved record.

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy requires MFA for all users
checks.Why: A password alone is enough to sign in for any account no policy asks for a second factor.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Add a Conditional Access policy that requires multifactor authentication for all users and all applications (Microsoft template: Require multifactor authentication for all users).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy requires MFA for admins
checks.Why: The 14 administrator roles Microsoft lists hold the keys to the tenant; each must be asked for a second factor.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Add a Conditional Access policy that requires multifactor authentication for every administrator role (Microsoft template: Require multifactor authentication for admins).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy requires MFA for Azure management
checks.Why: Azure management covers the Azure portal, CLI and PowerShell, where a signed-in account can change subscriptions.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Add a Conditional Access policy that requires multifactor authentication for Azure management (Microsoft template).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy blocks other legacy authentication clients
checks.Why: Legacy protocols (POP, IMAP, SMTP AUTH, older Office) cannot do MFA, so they are how password-spray attacks get in.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Add a Conditional Access policy that blocks legacy authentication for all users (Microsoft template: Block legacy authentication).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy blocks legacy authentication for Exchange ActiveSync
checks.Why: Exchange ActiveSync clients that use basic authentication bypass MFA the same way.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Include Exchange ActiveSync in the policy that blocks legacy authentication (Microsoft template: Block legacy authentication).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy covers the device code flow
checks.Why: Device code phishing relays a sign-in code to the victim, and MFA does not stop it; block the flow or require a managed device.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Add a Conditional Access policy that blocks the device code sign-in flow, excluding only devices that need it.

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy secures security info registration
checks.Why: Whoever registers the MFA method owns the account; registration from outside trusted locations should need a strong check.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Add a Conditional Access policy that protects registering MFA methods from outside your trusted locations (Microsoft template: Securing security info registration).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy requires MFA for guest access
checks.Why: Guests sign in with their home account; without this they reach your data on a password their organization controls.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Add a Conditional Access policy that requires multifactor authentication for guests and external users.

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device
checks.Why: Requiring a compliant (Intune-managed) device keeps data off unmanaged and personal devices.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1 + Intune
checks.Recommended: Add a Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant or hybrid joined device, or MFA, for all users, once devices are enrolled in Intune.

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy requires a compliant or hybrid joined device for admins
checks.Why: Administrators should work only from managed devices; a stolen admin session on a personal laptop is a full compromise.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1 + Intune
checks.Recommended: Require administrators to work from a compliant or hybrid joined device (Microsoft template).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy blocks unknown or unsupported device platforms
checks.Why: A sign-in from a platform you do not manage (for example ChromeOS or a spoofed client) slips past device-based policies.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Block sign-ins from device platforms your organization does not use or manage (Microsoft template).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy prevents persistent browser sessions on unmanaged devices
checks.Why: A browser that stays signed in on a shared or personal computer leaves the next person signed in as your user.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Stop browsers on unmanaged devices from staying signed in (Microsoft template: No persistent browser session).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy sets a sign-in frequency on unmanaged devices
checks.Why: Periodic reauthentication limits how long a session on an unmanaged device stays usable.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Ask for sign-in again periodically on unmanaged devices (Microsoft template: sign-in frequency).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy uses application enforced restrictions
checks.Why: Lets SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange give unmanaged devices a limited, web-only experience.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Use application enforced restrictions so SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange give unmanaged devices limited, web-only access.

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy requires MFA for risky sign-ins
checks.Why: A sign-in Microsoft rates medium or high risk (unfamiliar location, anonymous IP, token replay) should prove itself.
checks.LicenseRequirement: Entra ID P2
checks.Recommended: Require multifactor authentication when Microsoft rates a sign-in medium or high risk (needs Entra ID P2).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy requires a password change for high-risk users
checks.Why: A user Microsoft believes is compromised (for example a leaked password) should reset with MFA before signing in again.
checks.LicenseRequirement: Entra ID P2
checks.Recommended: Require a secure password change when Microsoft rates a user high risk (needs Entra ID P2).

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy targets all resources
checks.Why: A policy scoped to some apps leaves every other app reachable on whatever the default allows.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Have at least one Conditional Access policy that applies to all applications.

checks.Title: At least one Conditional Access policy targets all resources and all users
checks.Why: Microsoft recommends a baseline policy for all users and all resources with no app exclusions.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Have at least one Conditional Access policy that applies to all users and all applications.

checks.Title: A Conditional Access policy blocks high-risk agent identities
checks.Why: AI agents sign in on their own; an agent identity Microsoft rates high risk should be blocked.
checks.LicenseRequirement: Entra ID P2
checks.Recommended: Block AI agent identities that Microsoft rates high risk (Microsoft template: Block high-risk agent identities).

checks.Title: Every Conditional Access policy excludes the emergency access accounts
checks.Why: A misconfigured policy can lock out every administrator; the break-glass accounts are how you get back in.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Exclude your emergency access (break-glass) accounts from every Conditional Access policy, and record which accounts they are.

checks.Title: Conditional Access policies scoped to all users exclude the directory synchronization accounts
checks.Why: Microsoft Entra Connect signs in without MFA; an all-users policy that catches it stops directory synchronization.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Exclude the directory synchronization account role from policies that apply to all users.

checks.Title: Groups used in Conditional Access are protected (role-assignable or restricted management)
checks.Why: Anyone who can edit a group in a policy exclusion can take a user out of the policy.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Protect the groups your Conditional Access policies use (role-assignable groups or a restricted management administrative unit).

checks.Title: Every excluded user, group or role is included by another policy
checks.Why: An exclusion with no fallback leaves that object with no protection at all.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Make sure everyone excluded from one policy is covered by another.

checks.Title: No Conditional Access policy names a deleted group
checks.Why: A deleted group in an include list protects nobody; in an exclude list it hides a gap you can no longer see.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Remove deleted groups from your Conditional Access policies.

checks.Title: No Conditional Access policy names a user, group or role that no longer exists
checks.Why: A policy pointing at deleted objects may not apply the way it reads.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Remove deleted users, groups and roles from your Conditional Access policies.

checks.Title: User risk and sign-in risk are configured in separate policies
checks.Why: A policy with both conditions applies only when both are true, so neither risk is handled on its own.
checks.LicenseRequirement: Entra ID P2
checks.Recommended: Handle user risk and sign-in risk in separate Conditional Access policies.

checks.Title: Device registration MFA is not set in two places
checks.Why: When "Require MFA to register or join devices" is on in device settings, a Conditional Access policy on the register-device action is not enforced.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Require MFA for device registration in one place only: turn the device setting off when a Conditional Access policy handles it.

checks.Title: No Conditional Access policy uses the retired "Require approved client app" grant
checks.Why: Microsoft stopped enforcing this grant in March 2026; a policy relying on it no longer requires anything.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Replace the retired "Require approved client app" grant with "Require app protection policy".

checks.Title: Every Conditional Access policy targets at least one resource
checks.Why: A policy with no target resources has no effect even when it is on.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Give every Conditional Access policy at least one target application, or remove it.

checks.Title: Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policies are not left in report-only mode
checks.Why: Microsoft turns its managed policies on after review; one left in report-only protects nothing.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Review the Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policies and turn them on.

checks.Title: Regular users are blocked from legacy authentication (What If)
checks.Why: Entra itself evaluates an Exchange ActiveSync sign-in for a sample of users, including group membership the policy list cannot show.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Make sure an enabled Conditional Access policy blocks legacy authentication for every user.

checks.Title: Emergency access accounts are not blocked (What If)
checks.Why: Entra evaluates the same sign-in for each approved break-glass account; no policy should apply.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Make sure no Conditional Access policy applies to your emergency access accounts.

checks.Title: Regular users are asked for MFA in a browser (What If; the tool's addition)
checks.Why: Entra evaluates a browser sign-in to Exchange Online for the same sample; an enabled policy should require MFA or block.
checks.LicenseRequirement: M365 Business Premium or Entra ID P1
checks.Recommended: Make sure an enabled Conditional Access policy requires multifactor authentication for every user.

Policy.displayName: Require multifactor authentication for all users
Require multifactor authentication for Azure management

block-device-code.Note: Exclude any account that must use device code sign-in (for example Teams Rooms on Android) before turning it on.

secure-security-info.Note: Mark your office IP ranges as trusted named locations first; new users then register with a Temporary Access Pass.

Policy.displayName: Require multifactor authentication for guest access

compliant-hybrid-or-mfa.Note: Needs Intune compliance policies assigned to the devices before it can be turned on without blocking people.

Policy.displayName: Require compliant or hybrid joined device or MFA for all users

admin-compliant-device.Note: Every administrator needs an enrolled, compliant (or hybrid joined) device before this is turned on.

Policy.displayName: Require compliant or hybrid joined device for administrators

block-unknown-platforms.Note: Remove from excludePlatforms any platform your organization does not use, so it is blocked too.

Policy.displayName: Block access for unknown or unsupported device platforms
Require reauthentication and disable browser persistence on unmanaged devices

app-enforced-restrictions.Note: SharePoint applies it only after its unmanaged-device setting (Access control) is set to limited or blocked access.

Policy.displayName: Use application enforced restrictions for unmanaged devices

risky-user.Note: Users must be registered for MFA and self-service password reset first, or a high-risk user is blocked.

Policy.displayName: Require password change for high-risk users
